Report_ID: Pain intensity during maximum voluntary contraction (VAS 0-100 mm), 3 months

Author: Peterson, Butler, Eriksson & Svärdsudd
Comment: Means/SDs are crude (unadjusted) 3-month values from Table III; the reported p = 0.0005 comes from an adjusted multiple linear regression using all four measurement occasions, not from this simple 3-month between-group comparison. N analysed per arm was not restated for the pain outcome, so the numbers randomised (40 vs 41) were used. Baseline pain was higher in the exercise group. M_diff not computed to avoid sign-orientation ambiguity; means and SDs are provided.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Exercise group (3-month daily graded home exercise with weekly load increase + advice)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: adults aged 20-75 with tennis elbow symptoms >3 months

Report_ID: Pain severity in previous seven days (VAS /100) at 6 weeks
Title: Mobilisation with movement and exercise, corticosteroid injection, or wait and see for tennis elbow: randomised trial
Author: Bisset L, Beller E, Jull G, Brooks P, Darnell R, Vicenzino B
Comment: Paper reports the between-group difference as 'Physiotherapy - wait and see' = 15.6 (99% CI 4.7 to 26.4) with a positive score favouring physiotherapy; this has been INVERTED to treatment-minus-control orientation (M_diff = -15.6 on the 0-100 VAS, i.e. less pain with physiotherapy). SE_diff derived from the 99% CI width: (26.4 - 4.7)/5.15 = 4.21. Means/SDs are end-of-treatment values at 6 weeks (not change scores). Per-arm n analysed for the pain outcome is not separately stated; the 6-week analysed arm sizes shown in Table 3 (wait and see 60, physiotherapy 63) were used; randomised Ns were 67 and 66. Values are on a 0-100 mm VAS and require division by 10 for a 0-10 scale (not pre-converted here).
Design Type: randomised controlled trial (single blind, three-arm, pragmatic)
domain: musculoskeletal medicine / physiotherapy (lateral epicondylalgia, tennis elbow)
Participant type: Adults aged 18-65 with clinically diagnosed tennis elbow of at least six weeks' duration, no treatment by a health practitioner in the previous six months
Recruitment source: Community volunteers responding to advertisements and media releases, greater Brisbane region, Australia
Outcome measurement: Mean (SD) per group at 6 weeks and adjusted mean difference with 99% CI (Table 2)
Outcome variable: Pain severity in previous seven days (VAS /100) at 6 weeks
additional_group_ns: Corticosteroid injection arm (n=65 randomised; 6-week pain severity 16.4 (21.7)) excluded per synthesis plan (injection/drug comparator)

Report_ID: Pain most important complaint — mean improvement from baseline at 6 weeks (physical therapy vs brace only)
Title: Conservative Treatment of Lateral Epicondylitis: Brace Versus Physical Therapy or a Combination of Both—A Randomized Clinical Trial
Author: Struijs PAA, Kerkhoffs GMMJ, Assendelft WJJ, van Dijk CN
Comment: (1) Values are mean IMPROVEMENT (change) from baseline, not end-of-treatment pain scores — change scores were used for both arms (Table 3 title: "Mean Improvement (SD), Compared to Baseline"). (2) Because higher values = greater improvement, the reported MD of +13 FAVOURS physical therapy; on a raw pain-intensity scale this must be inverted (i.e. MD = -13 on the 0-100 pain scale, -1.3 on a 0-10 scale) before pooling. (3) SE_diff = (21-3)/3.92 = 4.59, derived from the reported 95% CI. (4) Group ns are the numbers randomised per arm (Table 3 headers); n analysed for pain at 6 weeks not separately reported (2 patients from A and 1 each from B and C were lost to follow-up). (5) IMPORTANT ELIGIBILITY CAVEAT: the comparator is an active brace-only (orthotic device) arm, NOT a minimal/no-intervention control; the authors explicitly state "A limitation of our trial was that no control group was included in our study." (6) Control arm n is shared with the combination-vs-brace row; if both rows are pooled, the brace n should be split (34 each).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Physical therapy (group A): 9 sessions over 6 weeks of pulsed ultrasound, deep friction massage, and progressive strengthening/stretching home exercise programme') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: adults with clinically diagnosed lateral epicondylitis of at least 6 weeks' duration
Recruitment source: general practitioners and primary care physical therapists referring to an outpatient clinic, urban setting
Outcome measurement: Mean improvement (SD) compared to baseline, Table 3; between-group mean difference with 95% CI (one-way ANOVA)
Outcome variable: Pain most important complaint — mean improvement from baseline at 6 weeks (physical therapy vs brace only)
additional_group_ns: Third arm not used in this row: Combination brace + physical therapy (group C), n = 56, mean improvement 24 (SD 31) at 6 weeks
outcome_units: points on an 11-point numeric rating scale (0-10) transformed to a 0-100 scale

Number analysed per arm for the pain outcome is not stated; the number randomised (12 per arm) was used - note the paper reports 10/24 (41%) dropout from the two physiotherapy-containing arms (5 physiotherapy alone, 5 physiotherapy plus injection), so analysed n is likely lower. M_diff not computed because the reported analysis is factorial.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Physiotherapy alone (Pienimaki progressive stretching/strengthening exercise programme)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); N-INCONSISTENCY: n_control(12) + n_treatment(7) = 19 ≠ n_total(24) — verify per-group Ns

Title: Augmented soft tissue mobilization vs natural history in the treatment of lateral epicondylitis: a pilot study
Author: Blanchette & Normand
Comment: Values are expressed as mean ± SD (Table 2 footnote). The paper does not explicitly state the VAS range or units, so outcome_units and scale min/max were left empty; the reported magnitudes (39-46 at baseline) are consistent with a 0-100 mm VAS and would require division by 10 for a 0-10 scale. No between-group test statistic for VAS at 6 weeks is reported (only a main effect of time and absence of a time × group interaction); M_diff = -5 was computed as experimental mean minus control mean at the 6-week timepoint (treatment minus control orientation). Group n's are the numbers analysed (15 experimental; 12 control after 3 control subjects were lost after randomization, per Fig 2) because per-arm n for the VAS outcome is not separately stated. Pilot study, underpowered.
Study Environment: biomechanics laboratory, Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières
Participant type: adults with clinically confirmed lateral epicondylitis (university employees)

Report_ID: Pain during the day — improvement from baseline at 6 weeks
Title: Corticosteroid injections, physiotherapy, or a wait-and-see policy for lateral epicondylitis: a randomised controlled trial
Author: Smidt N, van der Windt DAWM, Assendelft WJJ, Devillé WLJM, Korthals-de Bos IBC, Bouter LM
Comment: Table 3 reports IMPROVEMENT (change from baseline) means and SDs, not end-of-treatment absolute pain values; change scores were used for both arms. Higher values = greater improvement, so for a pain-intensity MD the sign must be inverted: physiotherapy minus wait-and-see = -6 points on 0-100 (= -0.6 on 0-10), favouring physiotherapy. SE_diff = (14 - (-2))/3.92 = 4.08 derived from the reported 95% CI of the mean difference in improvement. Ns are the numbers randomised per arm as reported in the table headers (per-arm n analysed for this outcome not separately stated).
Participant type: adults aged 18-70 with lateral epicondylitis of at least 6 weeks' duration recruited by family doctors
Recruitment source: 85 participating family doctors, primary care, five research centres
Outcome measurement: Mean (SD) improvement from baseline per arm on 0–100 transformed NRS; mean difference in improvement (95% CI)
Outcome variable: Pain during the day — improvement from baseline at 6 weeks
additional_group_ns: Corticosteroid injection arm (n=62) reported in the same table (improvement 47 [20] at 6 weeks) but excluded: an injection/drug comparator is not an eligible active arm under the synthesis plan.

Report_ID: Pain Score on VAS (0-100 mm) at 6 weeks
Title: Corticosteroid or placebo injection combined with deep transverse friction massage, Mills manipulation, stretching and eccentric exercise for acute lateral epicondylitis: a randomised, controlled trial
Author: Olaussen, Holmedal, Mdala, Brage, Lindbæk
Comment: Unadjusted group means/SDs at 6 weeks are taken verbatim from Table 3 (control 44 (25); placebo injection with physiotherapy 45 (23)) — note these differ from the study-detector summary which swapped the arms. M_diff is the paper's OWN adjusted GEE difference in estimated mean score (-3.7 mm, 99 % CI -12.4 to 5.0), already oriented as treatment minus control (negative favours the first-named treatment, i.e. physiotherapy); SE_diff derived as CI width / 5.15 = (5.0 - (-12.4))/5.15 = 3.3786 for the 99 % CI. Number analysed per arm for the VAS pain outcome is not reported, so numbers randomised (60 control, 58 placebo injection with physiotherapy) were used. All arms, including the control, received naproxen for the first 2 weeks. Values are on the 0-100 mm scale (divide means/SDs by 10 for a 0-10 scale).
Participant type: Adults aged 18-70 with clinically diagnosed acute lateral epicondylitis (symptom duration 2 weeks to 3 months)
Recruitment source: General practice (GP referrals), Sarpsborg, Norway, April 2009 - June 2012
Outcome measurement: Mean (SD) VAS pain score per group, plus adjusted GEE difference in estimated mean score with 99 % CI
Outcome variable: Pain Score on VAS (0-100 mm) at 6 weeks
additional_group_ns: Third arm not used for this comparison: corticosteroid injection with physiotherapy, n = 59 (extracted as a separate row); control n = 60 reported in full here rather than split across the two comparisons
